task.topic: Among patients undergoing diagnostic sampling of pulmonary lesions or mediastinal lymph nodes, does rapid on-site cytologic evaluation increase the probability of an adequate sample compared with no rapid on-site evaluation?

pico.population: Patients undergoing diagnostic sampling of pulmonary lesions or mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes
pico.exposure: Rapid on-site cytologic evaluation during sampling
pico.comparator: No rapid on-site cytologic evaluation during sampling

candidate_capture_policy.record_scope: Across all known-included reports, capture source-supported arm-level adequate-sampling records after ROSE versus no ROSE and preserve sampling modality and unit of analysis. Do not treat diagnostic yield, sensitivity, accuracy, procedure time, or complication outcomes as adequacy.

targets.quantitative_use_policy: Extract adequate-sample counts and denominators in both groups, the source adequacy definition, sampling modality, analysis unit, and a verified primary-source locator. Do not copy counts or effects from a review forest plot.

extraction.model_selection_policy: Preserve every source-reported candidate; no study or effect selection occurs in extraction.
extraction.evidence_requirements: Transcribe only source-supported data, preserve exact evidence, and do not calculate, pool, choose an analysis record, or infer missing values.
